title: Maximum Sum of K Consecutive Numbers
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the maximum sum of any consecutive subarray of length k.
think: What is the task asking? Find the best sum among all contiguous windows of size k.
What is the key operation? Reuse the previous window sum instead of recomputing from scratch.
What wording signals stand out? Maximum sum, consecutive, length k.
Which pattern fits? Sliding Window (fixed size).
What is the brute force idea? For each start index, sum k elements again.
What is the better/optimal idea? Keep a rolling window sum.
What are the edge cases? k = 1, k = nums.Length, negative numbers.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I add the new entering value and subtract the leaving value as the window moves.
algorithm: Compute sum of first k elements
For each new index from k to end
Update best if current sum is larger
interview: I would use a fixed-size sliding window. After the first window, I update the sum by adding the new element and subtracting the old one.
ru: Здесь ключевые слова — consecutive и size k. Это fixed sliding window.
visualExplanation:
nums = [2,1,5,1,3,2], k=3
window [2,1,5] sum=8
slide -> [1,5,1] sum=7
slide -> [5,1,3] sum=9 -> best

critical: Recompute each window sum from scratch and miss the pattern
nice: Do not mention fixed-size window explicitly

gaps: Nice to have: explain rolling sum fluently
whyThisPattern: This is a Sliding Window problem because we evaluate consecutive subarrays of fixed size k.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Two Pointers, because we are tracking a moving contiguous window, not comparing ends.
Not Prefix Sum as main pattern, because a rolling window is simpler here.
